I don't think the sasquatch is real.

The one thing that gives me a bit of pause is that both Teddy Roosevelt*, and Les Stroud had an encounter w something. Those are both experienced outdoors men, experienced w the American wilderness. Not saying that's proof, but kinda wierds me out.

*After looking a bit. It appears I am a little misinformed. Teddy recounted a tale told to him by another. He did not have an encounter himself. I thought I remember hearing he had, guess I was wrong, or heard inaccuracies.

There are many other experienced outdoorsmen who have had Sasquatch encounters, among countless hikers and campers who have also had similar encounters. The more you research this subject, the more you will find that many people have seen a similar bipedal cryptid described as being Sasquatch. Most people generally don't consider numerous eye-witness accounts proof, but in my opinion it is some proof that this creature exists.

To be fair, eye witnesses are very unreliable. This is shown repeatedly in studies. But an experienced outdoors man, and not a run of the mill hiker or camper, I take his word w a little more weight. People get spooked in the woods, making their testimony worse imho. but again, someone who knows the woods well, well I listen to them a bit more. I've always found the subject interesting either way.

Well, I don't think all eye witness accounts are unreliable, especially ones by other outdoorsman, and not all people imagine things. The studies claiming eye witness accounts are unreliable can be very biased against the Sasquatch subject. I agree, people get spooked in the woods and let their imagination get the best of them sometimes but I think generally people know what they're looking at and don't see things that aren't there. However, there are others who like to exaggerate or fabricate what they've seen too. That's why being an open-minded skeptic is necessary when researching this subject so that people can separate the falsehoods from the facts.
